summary: @c1-ease/bank ships install-time beacon to hardcoded VPS; stub package consistent with dependency-confusion probe
details: The package has no real functionality: its main export is a no-op Proxy that swallows all property access, described as a 'Compatibility shim.' The only behavior is a beacon in beacon.cjs that runs from scripts.postinstall ('node beacon.cjs') and also on require. The beacon POSTs host identifiers — hostname, install path, process.cwd(), and node/npm version — to a hardcoded endpoint at https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc with TLS certificate verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized:false). The scoped name @c1-ease/bank combined with the stub-plus-beacon shape and the collection of internal path/hostname fields is characteristic of a dependency-confusion reconnaissance package: any internal build pipeline that resolves this scoped name from the public registry instead of an internal one will leak internal host and filesystem metadata to the hardcoded third-party VPS.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
